idea-plugin.name: PHP Magic Method Navigation
idea-plugin.description:
Jump to the method PHP runs but never names. PHP calls some methods implicitly: a (string) cast or an echo quietly runs __toString(), $callable(...) runs __invoke(), and $obj->prop / $obj->method() fall through to __get() / __set() / __call() when the member is not really declared. None of these write the method's name, so Ctrl+Click and Go to Declaration have nothing to jump to. This plugin gives every one of those sites a gutter icon and a jump to the code that actually executes.

Reading the source, the call is invisible: echo $money; shows no method, yet it runs Money::__toString(); $discount(1999) looks like a function call but runs Discount::__invoke(); $obj->missing looks like a plain property read but runs __get(). You know the method exists, you just cannot get there without scrolling and searching by hand. The gutter icon closes that gap: click it and land on the method.

  • A gutter icon at every implicit site. A (string) cast, an echo / print, string interpolation ("$obj"), concatenation ("x" . $obj), a dynamic invoke ($callable(...)), and member access that resolves to no real member: $obj->prop read → __get(), $obj->prop = … → __set(), $obj->m(...) → __call(), Foo::m(...) → __callStatic(). When a union type (Money|Percentage) can dispatch to more than one implementation, the icon opens a multi-target popup.
  • Go to Declaration keeps working. Ctrl+Click / Ctrl+B on the operand offers the magic method alongside the normal jump, so you never lose the navigation you already rely on.
  • Reverse Find Usages. Run Find Usages on a magic method itself (e.g. __toString, __get, __call) and the results include the implicit sites that trigger it: the casts, the interpolations, the $obj->prop accesses that PhpStorm's own Find Usages never lists.
  • Precise, not noisy. Member access is marked only when the magic method really fires: a reference that resolves to a real declared property, constant, or method is left alone. It understands the \Stringable interface and nullable / union types (only the members that actually declare the method are offered), and it de-duplicates so nested and multi-argument sites never double-mark.
  • Yours to shape. A master switch plus a per-method toggle for __toString, __invoke, __get, __set, __call, __callStatic, and reverse Find Usages, under Settings | Tools | PHP Magic Nav.

Free, and staying free. Every feature above is free for any use, including commercial. There is no paid tier, no account, no telemetry: the plugin runs entirely inside your IDE and nothing about your code ever leaves your machine.

Built for PhpStorm, where the PHP language support ships in the box. It reuses the IDE's own type resolution to decide what runs, so a marked site is a site PHP would truly dispatch to a magic method.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• 0.2.2 - First stable-channel release. No functional changes from 0.2.1.
  • 0.2.1 - A read-modify-write on an undeclared property ($obj->prop += …, $obj->prop++) now offers both __get() and __set() - PHP reads the old value then writes the new one, so both fire. When two magic methods fire on the same operand (e.g. echo $obj->prop where __get returns a Stringable), the gutter marker now offers every jump instead of silently dropping one.
  • 0.2.0 - Member-access magic: gutter markers + Go to Declaration for __get()/__set() on undeclared $obj->prop read/write, and __call()/__callStatic() on undeclared $obj->m(...)/Foo::m(...) calls - only when the member does not resolve to a real declaration. Added reverse Find Usages: Find Usages on a magic method lists its implicit invocation sites. Per-method settings toggles for all six magic methods plus reverse Find Usages.
  • 0.1.0 - First release. Forward navigation to __toString() from casts, echo/print, interpolation and concatenation; navigation to __invoke() from dynamic $callable(...) calls; gutter markers + Go to Declaration; multi-target unions; settings toggles.
